summary: Intermittent 401 during token refresh in Private: signed session cookie HMAC mismatch correlated to MTU fragmentation on customer edge
description:
Issue summary:

Customers (Finlytics Inc) report intermittent 401 errors during background token refresh for private deployment behind their customer-managed edge. Error surface: 'invalid_session_signature' returned from identity-service during /token/refresh flow. Failures are short-lived (30s-90s) and recur across multiple hosts.

Impact:
- Several tenant users (admin+standard) experience failed token refreshes that force re-login in their apps.
- Affects production traffic in us-west region for Finlytics (private deployment).
- Customer is Tier: private with strict on-prem edge appliance.

Environment:
- Redwood Private control plane, identity-service v2.4.1, auth-proxy v1.9.3 running in customer VPC.
- Customer edge device: vendor "EdgeShield" appliance (firmware 3.2.7) performing TCP segmentation offload / path MTU adjustments.
- Region: prod/us-west (us-west-2).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Client token approaches expiry and client calls /token/refresh via auth-proxy.
2) Auth-proxy forwards signed session cookie in Cookie header to identity-service.
3) Identity-service returns 401 with log message 'signature verification failed: hmac mismatch' for ~0.5%-2% of requests intermittently.
4) After ~30-90s the same flow succeeds for same client without any change.

Observed logs and artifacts:
- Identity-service trace for failed request: correlation-id=abc123-prod-usw2-03, log: "signature verification failed: expected=... got=..."
- Auth-proxy debug shows Cookie header length truncated by ~40 bytes on failed requests (Cookie value truncated at end).
- Packet capture (pcap) from customer edge shows IP fragmentation and MSS clamping sequences correlating with time window of failures.
- No recent config changes on identity-service or auth-proxy in customer's control plane.

Hypothesis:
- Edge device performs MTU/MSS adjustments which cause large Cookie header values to be fragmented or truncated mid-transit; truncated cookie yields HMAC mismatch and identity-service rejects token. Intermittent because fragmentation only happens for longer cookie lengths or during pathological path MTU sequences.

Workaround provided to customer:
- Short term: Ask clients to use shorter session cookies (proposed session token compression/shorter metadata) OR disable cookie chunking on their edge. Finlytics applied an EdgeShield config to increase MSS and reported immediate reduction in failures.

Next steps / Action items:
- Support: continue monitoring for recurrence and collect additional correlation-ids.
- SRE/Serving: add defensive validation in auth-proxy to detect truncated cookie values and return 5xx to trigger client retry path (instead of returning 401) - design doc: link in comments.
- Engineering (identity-service): consider adding a graceful revalidation that fetches raw request bytes and attempts to reassemble fragmented cookie (limited scope).
- Customer success: coordinate with Finlytics network team for a permanent mitigation (edge firmware upgrade / config).

References:
- Slack thread: #support (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02SUPPORT/p1647012345000)
